Freight Rate Prediction

ML Engineering Assessment — Final Technical Report


Objective: predict posted freight rates for 12,000 future loads in November–December 2025 and generate the
required 31-day December scenario forecast.

1. Data Understanding & Quality
The labeled dataset contains 48,000 loads from January 1 through October 31, 2025. Key findings were 300
missing weights, 292 non-positive weights, and 374 missing market-index values. There were no duplicate rows or
duplicate load IDs. Non-positive weights are converted to missing and flagged rather than dropping affected loads.

Geographic consistency was checked with Haversine straight-line distance. The supplied route distances are
generally longer than geographic distance, which is consistent with road-network travel. A small upper tail of
distance/geodesic ratios was inspected rather than blindly removed.

2. Validation Strategy
Because the assessment is explicitly future-facing, a random split would not faithfully represent deployment.
Model selection used a chronological holdout: January–August 2025 for development training and
September–October 2025 for validation. After selection, the final model was retrained on all 48,000 labeled loads.

3. Feature Engineering
Features include Haversine distance, actual/geographic distance ratio, distance residual, log distance, log weight,
route identifier, equipment, month, day-of-week, day-of-year, weekend flag, elapsed time, market×quote
interaction, and quote-per-mile. Location, route, and equipment categoricals are handled natively by CatBoost.

4. Model Comparison

        Model                               MAE         RMSE           R²

          Linear Regression                                          $166.97          $712.86         0.7818

         Ridge                                                    $145.79          $646.75         0.8204

       Random Forest                                            $181.77          $663.50         0.8110

          Gradient Boosting                                          $134.41          $638.28         0.8251

        XGBoost                                                  $158.72          $654.36         0.8161

         CatBoost Direct Rate                                       $115.62          $634.23         0.8273

         CatBoost Rate-per-Mile                                    $100.80          $631.25         0.8289

        Ensemble 25/75                                           $102.17          $631.57         0.8287

MAE is the primary selection metric because it expresses average absolute pricing error directly in dollars and is less dominated by
extreme observations than RMSE.

5. Final Model
The selected model is CatBoost Rate-per-Mile. It predicts rate_per_mile = posted_rate / distance and reconstructs
predicted_rate = predicted_rate_per_mile × distance. This reduced chronological validation MAE to $100.80,
outperforming direct-rate CatBoost ($115.62 MAE) and the classical boosting baselines.

6. Productionization & Validation
The repository contains a reproducible training entry point, explicit feature construction, deterministic random
seeds, model-comparison artifacts, prediction generation, and the supplied scorer. The scorer successfully
validated 12,000 final predictions and 31 December predictions and generated the December chart.

7. Limitations & Next Steps
For production, I would add rolling-origin cross-validation, lane-level monitoring, feature drift detection, periodic
retraining, and a business cost-weighted error metric if pricing asymmetry is available. The assessment
configuration favors reproducibility and clear model selection over exhaustive hyperparameter search.
